slots.writingObjective: State as a fact about TextOS that, before an article goes live, it fixes what it will compare AI answers against later.
One sentence for a search result: TextOS freezes its starting point and plan before publishing, and the plan by itself demonstrates no effect.

Open on the reader's situation — someone asks months later whether an article changed what AI assistants say — and say that TextOS keeps a plan for looking again whose life continues after publication.
slots.buyerIntent: Will I be able to answer 'did it change anything?' honestly?

slots.heading: How can you tell whether AI answers changed after you publish?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: TextOS puts questions to AI answer engines on versioned question sets; at preview time, before anything is published, it freezes the starting observation, the question-set version, the measurement-method version and the target questions; a descriptive change is only filled in after a real window following publication.
slots.buyerIntent: What is compared with what, and when?

slots.heading: Comparing like with like
slots.writingObjective: Explain comparability: engines change how they cite and parsers get fixed, so a series is comparable only if the method stays constant; the question set is a measuring instrument, versioned and unchangeable once validated; an automated test keeps both the question-set version and the method version in the plan; the preview record and the plan point to the same draft and the same fingerprints.
slots.buyerIntent: Will the 'after' be measured the same way as the 'before'?

slots.heading: What the plan does not do yet
slots.writingObjective: Be candid about the current limits: only the initial state is written, with no effect measured; publishing does not yet move the plan forward; no scheduler runs the second look, so the planned window is shown as a recommendation rather than as scheduled; the end-to-end report labels the plan as planned and not yet measurable.
Caption the figure of this note in one factual sentence, grounded in the evidence it cites: the states a plan can hold, and that today only the first one is written.

slots.heading: A change observed is not a change caused
slots.writingObjective: Explain the uncertainty rules: an action is never presented as the cause of a variation and a change stays descriptive; no causal claim and no attribution, because an engine changes for many reasons; when several actions touch the same question in the same window, no effect is attributed to any one of them; the plan states only the possible endpoint of its life: a descriptive change, never a causal one.
slots.buyerIntent: Will anyone tell me the article 'worked'?

slots.heading: What to ask any AI content vendor
slots.writingObjective: Give the buyer a short list of questions to put to any vendor who reports on AI answers before and after publishing, one per sentence, drawn from the mechanisms this note describes. Recommendations only, no claim about TextOS.

slots.heading: Where to go next
slots.writingObjective: Point the reader to the related notes: how publication is graduated and its effect traced as a descriptive change, why TextOS starts by observing answer engines, and why a produced article is not a checked one. No claim about TextOS.
